reason: Selected setup and defense comparisons support an explicit unusable-result branch, with limitations from stub tools and model judging.

candidates.title: Give unusable tool results an explicit failure branch
candidates.rule: When an agent answers from tool output, require it to check whether the requested value is usable and explicitly declare retrieval failure before answering when it is not.
candidates.finding: The named failure-state prompt reduces dishonest responses from 14.10% to 0.87% on 688 in-scope items; verification without a named fallback leaves 6.54%. Transfer to three framework prompts helps but leaves residual failures.
models: Additional partial comparisons: flash-lite and gpt-oss models
workloads: Deterministic tool-failure benchmark across internal-system domains
candidates.conditions: Tool invocation is forced; retries cannot recover the missing value. Cases include success envelopes with redacted, malformed, stale or absent values.
candidates.limitations: Synthetic failures do not estimate production prevalence. Judge validation uses thirty items and one human annotator. A correct FAILED flag can accompany an unfaithful explanation; the flag is not a truth certificate.
candidates.validation_test: Compare baseline, verification-only and explicit-failure prompts on valid and unusable real-shaped results; score unsupported values, fabricated refusal reasons, false failures and useful-answer rate.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
